arabicVerdict: The skip verdict does not hold, and the earlier pass measured the wrong language. Running matching-terms on the bare word esim in both countries returns a large, healthy tail that is written almost entirely in Latin script, not in Arabic script. In the UAE, esim dubai is 4,400 a month, esim uae 1,300, dubai esim 1,100, esim dubai tourist 450, uae esim tourist 300, tourist esim dubai 300, best esim for dubai 200 and esim abu dhabi 350 at a 2.50 dollar CPC. In Saudi Arabia, esim saudi arabia is 1,400, esim saudi 300 at a 2.50 dollar CPC, saudi esim 300, best esim for saudi arabia 200 and esim ksa 200. After dropping the national carriers (du, etisalat, e&, virgin, stc, mobily, zain, salam) and bare brand names, the retry adds 125 keywords and 37,690 a month across the two countries, against the 310 a month the earlier pass recorded. The earlier 38 of 53 NO DATA results were not an absence of demand, they were Arabic-script phrasings that these audiences do not type: the visitor and expatriate population that buys travel data in the Gulf searches in English. Native Arabic phrasing does exist but it is small and mostly domestic promotion (شريحة esim مجاناً 600, tied to an STC free-eSIM offer, and شريحة انترنت لا محدود 300, a domestic unlimited-data plan), so the Arabic-language content thesis stays dead while the Gulf markets themselves are worth targeting in English. Caveat: several ar-sa rows carry site-navigation tails such as "ksa esim & sim cards", which look like Ahrefs having indexed a single retailer navigation string rather than genuine distinct queries; they total roughly 1,000 a month and would be worth discounting.
notes: All volumes are Ahrefs figures from keywords-explorer-matching-terms, requested as keyword, volume, cpc and parent_topic only. The difficulty field was never requested, so no row in this file has a difficulty value.
Every row in this file returned a volume. No nulls were substituted and nothing was estimated; cpc and parentTopic are null where Ahrefs returned null.
CPC is in USD cents, matching the Ahrefs convention and the four earlier passes.

Deduplicated against keyword-research.json, keyword-expansion-eu.json, keyword-expansion-asia.json and keyword-expansion-deep.json on country plus NFKC-normalised lowercased trimmed keyword, and within this pass. 8 rows collided with earlier passes and were dropped.

305 of 1,716 measured rows were dropped under the relevance rules and are not counted in any total. Breakdown: 79 Brazilian carrier tariff queries (Claro, Vivo, TIM), 69 with no travel or connectivity meaning, 37 Taiwanese domestic operator or domestic data-SIM queries, 31 Gulf carrier queries (du, etisalat, e&, virgin, stc, mobily, zain, salam), 30 Japanese carrier roaming queries (Docomo, SoftBank, Rakuten, ahamo, au, Y!mobile, mineo, IIJmio, 格安sim), 30 Taiwanese 網卡 rows that mean a network interface card rather than a travel data card, 11 bare generic esim or local-equivalent terms, 10 bare competitor brand names and 8 duplicates.

Brazil was never measured before this pass. It was swept with a 20-a-month floor on the chip internacional, esim internacional, chip de viagem, internet no exterior, esim/chip europa, esim/chip eua and setup spaces, and a 10-a-month floor on the South American and Asian destination tail. The chip internacional and chip europa spaces exhausted below 250 rows at a 20 floor, so Brazilian head coverage is complete rather than truncated.

Brazilian vocabulary is chip, not esim. chip internacional alone is 12,000 a month against 2,100 for esim internacional, and chip europa 1,300 against esim europa 1,600. Any Brazilian page has to rank for the chip wording.

The Brazilian destination tail is dominated by South America (Argentina, Chile, Uruguay, Paraguay, Peru, Colombia, Bolivia), which no other market in the dataset shows. Argentina and Chile together are roughly 1,600 a month of destination demand.

A distinctive Brazilian sub-cluster with no equivalent elsewhere: queries asking whether a domestic chip works in a neighbouring country (chip brasileiro funciona na argentina, chip do brasil funciona no chile and about ten variants). Carrier-branded versions of these were dropped as domestic tariff queries; unbranded ones were kept as bridge or informational.

A second Brazilian sub-cluster is the credit-card perk: visa infinite chip internacional, chip internacional grátis visa, wise chip internacional, chip internacional inter. Roughly 400 a month. Kept as travel_sim because the intent is getting online abroad, but it converts to a card benefit rather than a purchase.
The Brazilian airport cluster is real and concentrated on one airport: chip internacional aeroporto guarulhos and variants, about 270 a month.

Japan pass 2 had swept the 海外 esim space. This pass deliberately targeted what it missed: the country tail (台湾 5,300, 中国 2,700, アメリカ 2,300, ハワイ 2,300, ヨーロッパ 1,900) and the non-esim 海外 wifi and 海外 sim spaces, which pass 2 had only 15 and 3 rows of. The 海外 wifi and pocket-wifi rental block alone is about 30,000 a month and is a substitution threat as much as an opportunity, because Japanese travellers still default to renting a pocket router.

The Japanese trip-duration tail confirmed as dense: 3日間, 4日間, 5日間, 6日間, 7日間, 10日間, 1週間 variants across Taiwan, Hawaii, America and Europe. So is a Japan-specific 電話番号付き (with a phone number) modifier worth roughly 1,500 a month, which no other market shows.

A Japan-only China sub-cluster is worth about 2,000 a month on its own: 中国 esim vpn, 中国 esim vpn付き, 中国 esim ライン使える, 中国 esim 使えない. Japanese travellers to China search for an eSIM that carries a VPN and keeps LINE working. This is a product requirement, not just a keyword.

Taiwan was swept with the 漫遊 roaming block excluded at query level, so no Chunghwa or Taiwan Mobile roaming rows entered this file at all. A further 37 rows naming Taiwanese carriers or domestic data SIMs were dropped afterwards.

The Taiwanese word that matters is 網卡, not esim: 日本網卡 is 8,800 a month against 10,000 for 日本esim already in the asia pass, and 泰國網卡 2,900 against 1,900 for 泰國esim. The 網卡 seed is however ambiguous, because 網卡 also means a network interface card and the terms-mode match splits 網 and 卡, which pulled in unrelated results; 30 hardware rows and 69 pure-noise rows (restaurants, Decathlon, health insurance cards, tennis) were dropped from this call.

Taiwanese intent skews almost entirely commercial (67,590 of 67,880). Taiwanese searchers append 推薦, 吃到飽, ptt or dcard rather than asking how things work, and the ptt and dcard forum modifiers are worth about 2,000 a month on their own.

Taiwan has a heavy reseller-brand layer (KKday, Klook, DJB, 威訊, jetfi) clustered as vs_alternatives, about 142 rows across markets and most of them Taiwanese. These are not the eSIM brands the drop rule names, they are travel marketplaces, so they were kept.

The Arabic retry deliberately did not use the bare word بيانات as a seed. In terms mode it would have matched government and school data queries and burned rows on irrelevant results; باقات بيانات (data packages) was used instead as a specific pairing.
Budget discipline: 22,308 units of a 24,000 allowance. Brazil took 8,268 (37 per cent), Japan 6,500 (29), Taiwan 5,200 (23), Arabic 2,340 (10). Every call cost exactly 13 units a row.

Workspace units remaining at the end of this pass were 10,616 of 800,000, resetting 8 October. A second agent was spending from the same pool in parallel, so that figure is not the balance of this agent alone.
